chapterFiles.title: Isaiah 1 — Hear, O skies: the rebellious children, the worthless offerings, and the faithful city
Isaiah 2 — The mountain of the house of YHWH and the day against all that is lofty
Isaiah 3 — Jerusalem's leaders judged and the daughters of Zion stripped of their finery
Isaiah 4 — The branch of YHWH and the cloud and fire over Mount Zion
Isaiah 5 — The Song of the Vineyard and the six woes
Isaiah 6 — The throne-room vision and the prophet's commission
Isaiah 7 — The sign given to Ahaz: the two smoking firebrands, the young woman's son Immanuel, and the hired razor
Isaiah 8 — Maher-shalal-hash-baz, the waters of Shiloah and the River, and the sealed testimony
Isaiah 9 — The great light, the child born to us, and the hand stretched out still
Isaiah 10 — Woe to the makers of unjust decrees, Assyria the rod of anger, the returning remnant, and the march on Jerusalem
Isaiah 11 — The shoot from the stock of Jesse, the peaceable creatures, and the second gathering of the remnant
Isaiah 12 — The song of thanksgiving in that day: water drawn with joy from the wells of salvation
Isaiah 13 — The oracle concerning Babylon: the host from the end of the skies and the day of YHWH
Isaiah 14 — Israel restored and the taunt over the king of Babylon: the day star fallen from the heavens
Isaiah 15 — The oracle concerning Moab: the lament over the cities laid waste in a night
Isaiah 24 — The Little Apocalypse: the earth laid waste and the host of the height judged
Isaiah 25 — The song of the swallowed death: the banquet on the mountain and the fall of Moab
Isaiah 26 — The song of Judah and the dead who rise
Isaiah 27 — Leviathan slain, the vineyard restored, and the great trumpet of ingathering
Isaiah 29 — Woe to Ariel: the sealed scroll and the reversal of the deaf and the blind
Isaiah 32 — The king who reigns in righteousness: the noble and the fool, and the spirit poured from on high
Isaiah 40 — Comfort my people: the voice in the wilderness and the one who measured the skies
Isaiah 42 — The first Servant Song: my chosen one and the new song from the end of the earth
Isaiah 43 — You are my witnesses: created for my glory, the ransom of Israel and the new thing
Isaiah 44 — I am the first and the last: the idol-maker's block of wood, and Cyrus my shepherd
Isaiah 45 — Cyrus the anointed: the one who forms light and creates darkness, and the clay and the one who forms it
Isaiah 48 — Refined in the furnace of affliction: the new things created now, and the exodus from Babylon
Isaiah 53 — The fourth Servant Song: the suffering servant
Isaiah 54 — Sing, O barren one: the everlasting kindness and the covenant of peace
Isaiah 65 — I was found by those who did not seek me: the servants and the forsakers, and the new skies and the new earth

subtitles.en: The canon-cited chapters of Isaiah: the throne-room vision, the oracles against Babylon and Moab, the Little Apocalypse, the voice in the wilderness, the Servant Songs, Cyrus the anointed, and the new skies and the new earth

descriptions.en: Isaiah translated from the Hebrew in every chapter the Raëlian canon cites: **Isaiah 6** (the throne-room vision), **13–15** (the oracles against Babylon and Moab and the day star fallen from the heavens), **24–27** (the Little Apocalypse), **29** and **32**, **40–45** and **48** (the voice in the wilderness, the one who measured the skies, the Servant Songs, and Cyrus the anointed), **53** (the suffering servant), **54** and **65** (the new skies and the new earth). The rest of the book is not translated.

interlinearNote: Transliteration machine-generated from the pointed Hebrew (scripts/hebrew_translit.py, 2026-11-25): SBL academic consonants without spirantization, macrons for long vowels, dagesh forte doubled, maqqef as hyphen, YHWH for the divine name. Consistent but not hand-checked; shewa and qamets-qatan calls are heuristic.
